editorial:
Imagine waking up and finding out you committed a terrible crime, but you have absolutely no memory of doing it. That is exactly what happens to Mark Schall. He wakes up to find his mother-in-law dead and his father-in-law badly hurt. He turns himself in right away, but he is genuinely confused because he doesn't remember the attack. The movie feels like a classic courtroom drama mixed with a creepy mystery. You spend most of the time wondering if Mark is a cold-blooded killer pretending to be confused or if he really was just sleepwalking through a nightmare.

The acting is solid and keeps you guessing until the very end. The pacing is steady, though it feels a bit like an old TV movie, which gives it a cozy but tense vibe. If you like stories about legal loopholes and psychological twists, you will really enjoy this one. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend. You can find it streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for a crisp look, or you might want to rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch. If you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go.
endingExplained: In the end, the court has to decide if Mark was actually sleepwalking. The twist reveals that while he did have a history of sleep disorders, the evidence shows he was more aware than he claimed. It turns out his subconscious mind was acting on hidden anger toward his in-laws. He doesn't get off scot-free, and the movie wraps up by showing how the law handles these strange mental states.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves courtroom dramas and psychological mysteries.
